Name: Plaça de la Reina
Tips: ~11:20 THE MEETING POINT - agree it in advance and pin it. Works for both a train arrival (10-15 min walk from either station) and a bus arrival from Benidorm. OPTIONS B AND C ONLY - Sunday Aug 30.

Name: La Lonja de la Seda
Tips: 11:45 GO HERE FIRST - the 14:00 Sunday closing is the day's only hard door. UNESCO World Heritage 15th-century silk exchange: a hall of spiralling twisted stone columns fanning into palm-tree vaulting. The best thing in Valencia in 45 minutes, and free on Sundays.

Name: Plaça de la Verge
Tips: 12:35 - the cathedral apse, the Basílica dels Desemparats, the Turia fountain, café tables in the shade. Wander rather than tick; this is catching-up-with-your-friend time.

Name: Valencia Cathedral (Holy Grail)
Tips: SUNDAY HOURS 14:00-18:30 ONLY - collides head-on with the paella lunch. Pick one: rice or the Grail. If the cathedral wins, eat in the old town instead and go in at 16:00. Houses the Santo Cáliz, claimed as the Holy Grail.

Name: Mercat Central
Address: Plaça de la Ciutat de Bruges s/n, 46001 València
Tips: CLOSED SUNDAYS - do not walk here on Aug 30. One of Europe's great modernista market halls; it needs a weekday, so it is not happening this trip. Noted so nobody detours to a locked door.

Name: La Pepica
Tips: 14:00 LUNCH - THE PICK UNDER OPTION B. Beachfront since 1898, terrace facing the sea, Hemingway's table. Paella valenciana the orthodox way: chicken, rabbit, garrofó beans, saffron. SUNDAY 13:00-16:00. BOOK: +34 963 71 03 66. Rice is cooked to order, minimum 45 min, so a 14:00 table eats ~14:45 - that is normal.

Name: La Marcelina
Tips: VALUE ALTERNATIVE next door to La Pepica - older still, founded 1888, same sea view and same rice tradition, noticeably cheaper. The call if five people at 40 EUR each stings. SUNDAY 11:00-16:00. Book: +34 963 71 20 25.

Name: Casa Carmela
Tips: DO NOT PLAN FOR THIS ON A SUNDAY - CLOSED SUNDAYS, and no dinner service on any day. The connoisseur's orange-wood-fired paella, kitchen 13:00-16:00 Mon-Sat only. Listed so it is not mistakenly chosen.

Name: Platja de la Malvarrosa
Tips: 16:15 - swim and walk it off with your friend. Wide, clean, shallow, lifeguarded, showers along the promenade, sea ~25 C in late August. PACK SWIMWEAR AND A CHANGE OF CLOTHES IN A DAY BAG - there is no hotel to go back to. This is the Barceloneta afternoon, relocated. Blue-zone parking here is FREE on Sundays.

Name: El Palmar (Albufera)
Tips: OPTION C ONLY - THE WHOLE ARGUMENT FOR RENTING A CAR. The birthplace of paella: a fishing village on stilts in the Albufera lagoon, 15 km / 20-25 min south of Valencia on the V-15, ~25 restaurants cooking rice over orange-wood fires. Effectively unreachable by public transport on a day-trip schedule. BOOK THE TABLE and arrive before 14:00: parking is normally free and plentiful EXCEPT summer Sunday lunchtimes, which is exactly when you would arrive.

Name: Albufera boat pontoon (El Palmar)
Tips: OPTION C - flat wooden albuferencs leave the pontoon all day for a 30-40 min circuit of the lagoon and the Gola canal, through rice fields and waterfowl. Sunset (~20:15 on Aug 30) is the best hour in the province but sits past your departure - take the afternoon circuit, or trade the beach for it.

Name: Ciutat de les Arts i les Ciències
Address: Av. del Professor López Piñero 7, 46013 València
Tips: WET FALLBACK - Calatrava's white spaceship complex, 15 min from the old town. The Oceanogràfic is Europe's largest aquarium, open daily and entirely indoors. Rain kills only the beach half of the day; this plus the cathedral replaces it.

Name: València Joaquín Sorolla station
Address: Carrer de San Vicente Mártir 171, 46007 València
Tips: OPTION B - Euromed's normal terminus. ~800 m / 15 min walk south of the old town, free shuttle bus to València Nord. ON RENFE'S FORM SELECT 'VALENCIA (TODAS)', NOT A NAMED STATION - platform works pushed Euromed to València Nord from 6 May 2025 to 30 June 2026 and overruns are routine. Check the return leg departs from wherever you arrived.

Name: València Nord station
Tips: OPTION B - the 1917 modernista station right at Plaça de l'Ajuntament, ~10 min walk to Plaça de la Reina. The BETTER outcome if Euromed is still routed here. NEVER book València Cabanyal - regional trains only, 3 km out.

Name: Estació d'Autobusos de València
Tips: YOUR FRIEND ARRIVES HERE. ALSA Benidorm to Valencia is direct 1h45 and runs roughly hourly (28 services/day). There is NO useful rail from Benidorm - the FGV tram only runs down the coast to Alicante. Hourly service means a missed bus costs him an hour not the day. Short taxi or metro from here to Plaça de la Reina.

Name: Sixt Barcelona Sants
Address: SABA Sants Estació level -1, Plaça dels Països Catalans s/n, 08014 Barcelona
Tips: OPTION C PICKUP - THE PICK. Open daily 07:00-23:00 (NOT 24/7 - only the airport branch is). Metro L5 direct from the flat, and it is where Monday's AVE leaves from. From Plaça de Joan Peiró take the lift to -1, just past the McDonald's. Collect 07:00-07:30. WARNING: returning at 22:45 leaves ~15 min against the 23:00 close - either leave Valencia by 18:45 or use the Eixample branch's 24-hour key drop. Sixt Spain: 902 49 16 16.

Name: Sixt Barcelona Centre/Eixample
Tips: OPTION C ALTERNATIVE - closest branch to the flat and the ONLY one whose 24-hour key drop covers a post-midnight return. Hours Mon-Fri 08:00-20:00, Sat-Sun 08:00-16:30, 24-hour return. REPORTED UNDER RENOVATION with pickups redirected to Sants - verify when booking. Do NOT plan to return the car Monday morning: you leave the flat at 09:40 for an 11:00 AVE.
